issue.title: [agent-runtime 03/08] Implement Semp-only delegation with a session registry (#229)

body:

Branch: `bb/relay-229-agent-runtime-03-08-implement-semp-onl-thr_pi754evzrm`

## Summary

Implements issue #229 in `backend/packages/agent-runtime`:

- **`delegationRegistry.ts`** — `DelegationRegistry`, a process-memory registry of open supervisor→project-agent delegated sessions keyed by `(supervisorRunId, targetProjectItemId)`. A first delegation onto a key opens an `agent_runs` row (`unit='session'`, `triggeredBy='supervisor'`) and an in-process `AgentSession`; a further delegation within 24 hours reuses the same session as a new turn. A duplicate call onto a key already mid-turn is rejected immediately with a fixed busy `tool_result` message, never blocking or overwriting the in-flight call. Busy-check and reservation of a brand-new key both happen synchronously (before any `await`), which closes the race where two concurrent calls onto the same new key would otherwise both try to create a session. After 24 hours of inactivity an in-process timer discards the entry and closes its run as `done` — no backing table or job.
- **`delegateTool.ts`** — `createDelegateTool` wraps the registry as the `agentTool.delegate` handler, returning only the target's final message (or the busy error) as a `tool_result`-shaped value. Restricting this tool to Semp's own manifest is left to the not-yet-built composition root (#91), the same pattern `startupRepair.ts` used for its own missing caller.
- **`lifecycleAdapter.ts`** — extracted the turn-processing loop into a reusable `runAgentTurn`, so `runAgentSession` (one turn, closes the run) and the new registry (many turns, closes only on TTL) share identical event bookkeeping.
- **`types.ts`** — added an optional `AgentSession.send()` continuation method for reusing an open session across turns.

The branch was rebased onto `origin/develop` to pick up the already-merged parts 01/08 and 02/08.

Verification this run: `pnpm run build` (clean, all 9 packages), `test:unit` (83/83), `test:integration` (441/441, including 8 new tests for the registry and tool), `test:e2e` (5/5), and `check:boundaries` (no violations) — all green.

## Summary

Addressed the code review findings from the failed `code-review` CI check on PR #322:

**High severity (2, fixed)**
- `DelegationRegistry.delegate()` now catches errors from `runAgentTurn` in both the new-session and reused-session branches, closing the `agent_runs` row as `error` (matching `runAgentSession`'s existing pattern) and dropping the broken entry from the registry, instead of leaving the row stuck at `running` forever.
- `scheduleTtl`'s TTL callback no longer silently drops a rejection: `expire()` now catches its own DB failures internally, logs them, and reschedules a retry instead of losing track of the entry.

**Medium severity (3, fixed)**
- Added a well-formed-UUID validation on `targetProjectItemId` before it reaches `createAgentRun`'s SQL, since it originates from the model's own untrusted tool-call arguments.
- Removed the unused, untested `systemPromptOverride` field from `DelegateInput` (out of issue #229's scope).
- Stopped re-exporting `runAgentTurn`, `extractResultSnapshot`, `pushRunStatus` from the package's public `index.ts` — kept as internal helpers only.

**Low priority**
- Fixed the `delegateTool.test.ts` blocking fixture to yield `turn_end`.
- Documented why `lastActivityAt` is kept even though not read internally (issue #229 requires it as an entry field).
- Added 3 new tests for UUID rejection and error-path cleanup.

Verified this run: `pnpm run build` (clean), `test:unit` (83/83), `test:integration` (444/444), `test:e2e` (5/5), `check:boundaries` (no violations) — all green.

## Summary

Addressed the last open medium-severity finding from the code review on PR #322:

**Missing cleanup on send-falsy error path (fixed)**: In `DelegationRegistry.delegate()`'s reused-session branch, the check for `existing.session.send` being missing threw *before* the inner `try/catch` that performs the three-step cleanup (delete entry, clear TTL timer, `failRun`). That left the broken entry in the registry with `busy` reset to `false`, so every subsequent delegation onto that key would hit the same throw until the TTL eventually fired and closed the row as `done` instead of `error`. Moved the check inside the inner `try` so a session that can't continue now goes through the exact same cleanup path as a turn that throws mid-flight.

Added a new test verifying the run is closed as `error` with the expected message, the entry is fully removed from the registry, and a fresh delegation onto the same key succeeds afterward.

Verified this run: `pnpm run build` (clean), `test:unit` (83/83), `test:integration` (445/445, +1 new test), `test:e2e` (5/5), `check:boundaries` (no violations) — all green.
